subject: Aurora - Livechat high-latency incident: interim mitigations & post-incident summary
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@aurora.co>, Aurora Support <support@aurora.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora - Livechat high-latency incident (Mar 15) — immediate guidance

Hi Jordan / Aurora team,

Quick update from the Redwood side — between 07:45 and 08:05 PT we observed an elevated tail-latency affecting streaming/chat endpoints used by your livechat integration (manifested as delayed token emission and intermittent stalls). Customers on mobile clients reported the highest visible impact (longer streaming gaps, occasional UI timeouts).

What we're doing now:
- Routing new requests to warm standby replicas to reduce edge queueing.
- Temporary autoscale bump to increase concurrency on the regions serving your traffic.
- Short-term kernel rollback to the last stable streamer (no model change) while we validate the mitigation.

Immediate actions you can take (low-risk, quick):
- Enable chunked streaming and max_tokens=256 on the client to reduce single-request token bursts.
- Implement a 300ms client-side retry for the streaming socket (idempotent resume); prefer a capped exponential backoff.
- If you have a mobile-only toggle, shift heavy assistant responses to a shorter summarization model (we can help pick a profile).

Attachments: incident-telemetry-snippet.txt (small telemetry extract), aurora-multipath-playbook.pdf (short playbook).

We opened INC-7623 and will update this thread as we confirm fixes. I know livechat is critical for your support flows — we will prioritize.

Next steps: Ben and Irene are investigating root cause; I'll send a concise post-incident summary within 48 hours and share a timeline + recommended durable fixes.

If you want a quick sync now, I can jump on a 15-min call.

— Stephanie

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:05:42 -0700
Subject: Re: [Internal] Aurora - Livechat high-latency incident (Mar 15) — immediate guidance

Internal findings so far (short):
- Telemetry shows a microburst of concurrent long-running requests causing head-of-line queueing on the edge proxy cluster in us-west-2.
- The streamer kernel change deployed last night introduced a path that increases memory pressure under certain token cadence patterns; we see elevated GC + blocked IO windows correlated with the latency spikes.
- Warm replicas handled most traffic, but a subset of front proxies accumulated backlog for ~90s before failover.

Immediate engineering plan:
1) Roll the streamer kernel back to the previous stable build for affected pools (already initiated).
2) Add a short-lived queuing limit on the edge proxy (300 concurrent) to prevent head-of-line contention.
3) Tune autoscaler thresholds to react faster to token-burst patterns (reduce scale-up window).
4) Add a telemetry counter and alert for >50% of requests showing token emission gaps >250ms.

User-visible mitigations we've recommended to Aurora (in the external message): chunked streaming, lower max_tokens, small client-side retry. These are low friction and should reduce the worst customer-visible symptoms while we finish the rollback and infra tune.

I'll push an updated incident log to INC-7623 and attach a short snippet for Aurora. ETA for rollback confirmation: ~30–45 minutes from now.

— Ben

Subject: Aurora - Livechat incident postmortem and durable mitigations (Mar 15)

Jordan — thanks again for your patience. Below is a concise post-incident summary plus recommended next steps. Attached: aurora-incident-postmortem.pdf (full write-up).

Summary (what happened)
- Between 07:45 and 08:05 PT on Mar 15, an emergent token-cadence pattern from a subset of long-running assistant messages combined with a recently deployed streamer kernel optimization produced elevated memory pressure on edge proxies. The pressure created short periods of blocked IO which in turn caused delayed token emission and intermittent streaming stalls for some sessions. Mobile clients were disproportionately affected due to longer single-request token windows.

Impact
- Estimated impact window: 20 minutes.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/stream and related streaming websockets.
- Customer-visible: increased tail latency and occasional socket stalls for ~8–12% of sessions at peak.

Root cause
- Regression introduced by a streamer kernel optimization when interacting with token-cadence-heavy requests; combined with insufficient proxy queuing limits under burst conditions.

Mitigations taken (what we did)
- Rolled back the kernel change for affected pools within ~45 minutes.
- Increased autoscale headroom for us-west-2 and added warm standby routing.
- Implemented a short-term proxy concurrency cap to prevent head-of-line queuing.
- Issued client-side guidance (chunked streaming, reduced max_tokens) to reduce request burstiness.

Durable fixes (planned)
- Patch streamer kernel to eliminate GC path that interacts poorly with token-cadence patterns (target: 2 weeks).
- Permanent proxy-level rate limiting and smarter request prioritization (target: 1 month).
- Improve autoscaler heuristics to detect token-cadence spikes and scale faster (target: 3 weeks).

What we recommend for Aurora (actionable)
- Enable chunked streaming where possible (server-side switch available; we can help validate client behavior).
- Set client max_tokens to 256 for mobile builds until we finish kernel patching.
- Optional: add a lightweight summarization layer for mobile clients for long assistant responses.

Make-good and next steps
- We will extend a one-time service credit equivalent to two days of streaming usage for the impacted time window; your account manager will follow up.
- Offer: 45-minute run-through with our SRE and platform engineering to go over architecture and prioritized mitigations.
- I will add links to the full telemetry export and the incident ticket: INC-7623 and https://drive.redwood.com/aurora/incident-2027-03-15.

Please let me know if you'd like us to schedule the follow-up technical session — available times below.

Times I can offer (PDT): Thu Mar 18 09:00–12:00 or Thu Mar 18 15:00–17:00. If those don't work, propose alternatives and we'll accommodate.

Apologies again for the disruption — we take incidents like this seriously and will keep you updated on the durable fixes.

Best,
— Stephanie Nguyen
